readmeHtml:
Oat UI

Semantic, minimal, zero dependencies. ~10KB CSS and JS.

Oat is an ultra-lightweight HTML + CSS, semantic UI component library with zero dependencies. No framework, build, or dev complexity. Just include the tiny CSS and JS files and you are good to go building decent looking web applications with most commonly needed components and elements.

Semantic tags and attributes are styled contextually out of the box without classes, forcing best practices, and reducing markup class pollution. A few dynamic components are WebComponents and use minimal JavaScript.

I wrote this to use in my own projects after getting sick of the ridiculous bloat, dependencies, and rug-pulls in Javascript UI/component libraries.

See live demo and docs at oat.ink

aiSummary.oneLiner: An ultra-lightweight, zero-dependency HTML and CSS component library enforcing semantic markup.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Oat UI is a highly minimalistic frontend component library that operates entirely without complex build steps or dependencies. Weighing in at under 10KB total for both CSS and JS, it provides a clean, attractive default styling for standard HTML elements. It heavily enforces semantic web practices by styling raw HTML tags and attributes contextually, rather than relying on massive utility classes or complex React wrappers. The few dynamic interactive components it offers are implemented entirely as native Web Components. It is explicitly designed as a massive rejection of the bloat and extreme complexity currently dominating the JavaScript framework ecosystem.
keyFeatures: Zero dependencies: Operates perfectly out of the box without requiring npm, build steps, or JavaScript frameworks.
Semantic styling: Contextually styles native HTML elements rather than polluting the markup with hundreds of utility classes.
Native Web Components: Uses lightweight, standard browser Web Components for the few elements requiring dynamic JavaScript interaction.
Tiny footprint: Keeps total bundle size incredibly small (under 10KB), maximizing page load speed and performance.
Drop-in simplicity: Requires only a single CSS file and a single JS file to start building beautiful, fully functional web applications.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Frontend developers and full-stack engineers exhausted by modern Javascript UI bloat who want a completely minimal, semantic, and dependency-free way to style web applications. Familiarity with component-library workflows is highly recommended for optimal usage.
aiSummary.gettingStarted: Just include the tiny CSS and JS files in your HTML.
